entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Volusius Saturninus was a Roman Senator who played a crucial role in the Roman Empire during the Principate. He was consul in the year 56 alongside Publius Cornelius Scipio, showcasing his significance as a key figure in Roman politics. Saturninus's influence extended beyond his term in office, as he contributed to the development of Roman law and governance.

As a senator, Saturninus was part of a larger network of influential individuals who shaped the Roman Empire's trajectory. His legacy can be seen in the continued development of Roman law and governance, which had a lasting impact on Western civilization.

The Roman Empire's legacy is a testament to the enduring influence of Saturninus and his contemporaries. Despite the passing of centuries, their contributions to Roman politics, law, and governance remain relevant today.

In the annals of Roman history, Quintus Volusius Saturninus stands as a testament to the power of individual agency and collective effort in shaping the course of human civilization.
